lead: Z parameters describe a two-port by writing its two port voltages in terms of its two port currents. Y parameters do the opposite: they write the two port currents in terms of the two port voltages. The Z set is measured with one port open, the Y set with one port shorted, and for the same network the Y matrix is the inverse of the Z matrix. Z parameters are the natural choice when two-ports are joined in series, Y parameters when they are joined in parallel, and both are the starting point for every other parameter set.
prereq: You need the port variables and the sign convention from two-port concept and terminology, impedance and admittance of R, L and C, and the inverse of a 2 × 2 matrix.

blocks.text: Take the two port currents I₁ and I₂ as the free variables. Because the network is linear, each port voltage is a weighted sum of the two currents:
V₁ = z₁₁I₁ + z₁₂I₂,   V₂ = z₂₁I₁ + z₂₂I₂
blocks.where: where z₁₁, z₁₂, z₂₁ and z₂₂ are the Z parameters, all in ohms; in matrix form [V] = [Z][I].

blocks.text: To isolate one parameter, make the other current zero by leaving that port open. With port 2 open (I₂ = 0), z₁₁ = V₁/I₁ is the input impedance and z₂₁ = V₂/I₁ is the forward transfer impedance. With port 1 open (I₁ = 0), z₂₂ = V₂/I₂ is the output impedance and z₁₂ = V₁/I₂ is the reverse transfer impedance. Every Z test uses an open circuit, so they are called open-circuit impedance parameters.
The subscripts follow one rule: the first index is the port where the response is read, the second is the port that is driven.
Now take V₁ and V₂ as the free variables:
I₁ = y₁₁V₁ + y₁₂V₂,   I₂ = y₂₁V₁ + y₂₂V₂
blocks.where: where the y parameters are in siemens (S); in matrix form [I] = [Y][V].

blocks.text: To make a voltage zero, short that port. With port 2 shorted (V₂ = 0), y₁₁ = I₁/V₁ is the input admittance and y₂₁ = I₂/V₁ is the forward transfer admittance. With port 1 shorted (V₁ = 0), y₂₂ = I₂/V₂ and y₁₂ = I₁/V₂. These are the short-circuit admittance parameters. In a passive network y₂₁ is usually negative: with port 2 shorted, current flows out of terminal 2 into the short, and I₂ is defined entering.
Both sets describe the same box. Substituting [V] = [Z][I] into [I] = [Y][V] gives [Y] = [Z]⁻¹, so
y₁₁ = z₂₂/Δz,  y₁₂ = −z₁₂/Δz,  y₂₁ = −z₂₁/Δz,  y₂₂ = z₁₁/Δz
blocks.where: where Δz = z₁₁z₂₂ − z₁₂z₂₁ is the determinant of [Z], in Ω². The same rule run backwards gives z₁₁ = y₂₂/Δy, z₁₂ = −y₁₂/Δy, z₂₁ = −y₂₁/Δy, z₂₂ = y₁₁/Δy with Δy = y₁₁y₂₂ − y₁₂y₂₁ in S².

blocks.text: The diagonal terms swap places, and both off-diagonal terms change sign. z₁₂ is not 1/y₁₂: the inverse of a matrix is not the matrix of reciprocals.

sections.h3: Which set exists, and which to use

items: A T network (series arms Z₁, Z₂, shunt arm Z₃) gives its Z parameters by inspection: z₁₁ = Z₁ + Z₃, z₂₂ = Z₂ + Z₃, z₁₂ = z₂₁ = Z₃. A π network (shunt arms Y<sub>A</sub>, Y<sub>C</sub>, series arm Y<sub>B</sub>) gives its Y parameters by inspection: y₁₁ = Y<sub>A</sub> + Y<sub>B</sub>, y₂₂ = Y<sub>B</sub> + Y<sub>C</sub>, y₁₂ = y₂₁ = −Y<sub>B</sub>.

If Δz = 0 no Y matrix exists. A lone series impedance Z between terminals 1 and 2 has no Z matrix but has y₁₁ = y₂₂ = 1/Z, y₁₂ = y₂₁ = −1/Z; a lone shunt impedance has a Z matrix (all four entries Z) but no Y matrix; an ideal transformer has neither. The ABCD parameters handle all three.
Z suits series connections and Y suits parallel connections; see interconnection of two-ports. Equal off-diagonal terms (z₁₂ = z₂₁) mark a reciprocal network; see symmetry and reciprocity.

figure.caption: The two tests on the T network. With port 2 open, 1 A gives 6 V at port 1 and 4 V at port 2 (z₁₁ = 6 Ω, z₂₁ = 4 Ω). With port 2 shorted, 1 V drives 0.2692 A in and 0.1538 A out of terminal 2 (y₁₁ = 0.2692 S, y₂₁ = −0.1538 S).

spec.aria: Two circuit panels of the 2, 3, 4 ohm T network. Top: a 1 A source at port 1 with port 2 open gives V1 = 6 V and V2 = 4 V. Bottom: a 1 V source with port 2 shorted gives I1 = 0.2692 A and 0.1538 A flowing out of terminal 2 into the short.

examples.question: A T network has series arms Z₁ = 2 Ω (port 1 side) and Z₂ = 3 Ω (port 2 side) and a shunt arm Z₃ = 4 Ω to the common terminal. (a) Find the Z parameters from the open-circuit tests. (b) Find Δz and the Y parameters. (c) Check y₁₁ and y₂₁ directly with port 2 shorted and 1 V applied at port 1.
steps: Port 2 open (I₂ = 0): no current in Z₂, so I₁ flows through Z₁ and Z₃. V₁ = I₁(2 + 4) = 6I₁, so z₁₁ = 6 Ω. V₂ is the drop across Z₃ (no drop on the idle Z₂): V₂ = 4I₁, so z₂₁ = 4 Ω.
Port 1 open (I₁ = 0): I₂ flows through Z₂ and Z₃. V₂ = I₂(3 + 4) = 7I₂, so z₂₂ = 7 Ω, and V₁ = 4I₂, so z₁₂ = 4 Ω.
Direct check: with port 2 shorted, Z₂ ∥ Z₃ = 3 × 4/7 = 1.7143 Ω, so the input resistance is 2 + 1.7143 = 3.7143 Ω and I₁ = 1/3.7143 = 0.2692 A. Then y₁₁ = I₁/V₁ = 0.2692 S ✓.
Centre-node voltage = 1 − 2 × 0.2692 = 0.4615 V. The current through Z₂ into the short is 0.4615/3 = 0.1538 A, leaving terminal 2, so I₂ = −0.1538 A and y₂₁ = I₂/V₁ = −0.1538 S ✓.
examples.answer: z₁₁ = 6 Ω, z₁₂ = z₂₁ = 4 Ω, z₂₂ = 7 Ω; Δz = 26 Ω²; y₁₁ = 0.2692 S, y₁₂ = y₂₁ = −0.1538 S, y₂₂ = 0.2308 S, confirmed by the short-circuit test.

examples.question: A π network has a 2 Ω shunt resistor across port 1, a 4 Ω series resistor between terminals 1 and 2, and a 5 Ω shunt resistor across port 2. Find its Y parameters by inspection, then its z₁₁ and z₂₂, and check them by series-parallel reduction.
steps: Admittances: Y<sub>A</sub> = 1/2 = 0.5 S, Y<sub>B</sub> = 1/4 = 0.25 S, Y<sub>C</sub> = 1/5 = 0.2 S.
y₁₁ = Y<sub>A</sub> + Y<sub>B</sub> = 0.75 S; y₂₂ = Y<sub>B</sub> + Y<sub>C</sub> = 0.45 S; y₁₂ = y₂₁ = −Y<sub>B</sub> = −0.25 S.
Check z₁₁: with port 2 open, port 1 sees 2 Ω in parallel with (4 + 5) Ω: 2 × 9/11 = 1.6364 Ω ✓. Check z₂₂: port 2 sees 5 Ω in parallel with (4 + 2) Ω: 30/11 = 2.7273 Ω ✓.
examples.answer: y₁₁ = 0.75 S, y₁₂ = y₂₁ = −0.25 S, y₂₂ = 0.45 S; z₁₁ = 1.6364 Ω and z₂₂ = 2.7273 Ω, matching the direct reductions.

traps: z₁₁ is measured with port 2 open, not shorted. For the T network, shorting port 2 gives 3.7143 Ω, not z₁₁ = 6 Ω; 3.7143 Ω is 1/y₁₁.
z₁₂ is not 1/y₁₂. Here z₁₂ = 4 Ω but 1/y₁₂ = 1/(−0.1538) = −6.5 Ω. Invert the whole matrix.

The off-diagonal terms change sign in the inversion: y₁₂ = −z₁₂/Δz. Writing +z₁₂/Δz gives y₂₁ = +0.1538 S, which says current enters terminal 2 from the short, which is impossible for a passive network driven at port 1.
Units: z in ohms, y in siemens, Δz in Ω², Δy in S². A determinant written in plain ohms is marked wrong.
Not every network has both sets: a lone series element has no Z matrix and a lone shunt element has no Y matrix.

quiz.q: Define z₁₂ and give its test condition and unit.
quiz.a: z₁₂ = V₁/I₂ with I₁ = 0 (port 1 open, port 2 driven). Unit: ohm. It is the voltage at port 1 per ampere driven into port 2.

quiz.q: For the T network, y₂₁ = −0.1538 S. Explain the minus sign physically.
quiz.a: With port 2 shorted and port 1 driven, current flows through Z₂ out of terminal 2 into the short. I₂ is defined entering terminal 2, so it is negative, and y₂₁ = I₂/V₁ is negative.

quiz.q: A two-port has z₁₁ = 10 Ω, z₁₂ = z₂₁ = 5 Ω, z₂₂ = 20 Ω. Find Δz and all four y parameters.
For the T network of the first worked example, find the impedance seen at port 2 with port 1 shorted, and compare it with z₂₂.
quiz.a: With port 1 shorted, Z₁ ∥ Z₃ = 2 × 4/6 = 1.3333 Ω; add Z₂: 4.3333 Ω. It equals 1/y₂₂ = 26/6 = 4.3333 Ω, not z₂₂ = 7 Ω (which needs port 1 open).

quiz.q: For a T network with arms Z₁, Z₂, Z₃, show that Δz = Z₁Z₂ + Z₂Z₃ + Z₃Z₁, and use it to check the first worked example.
quiz.a: Δz = (Z₁ + Z₃)(Z₂ + Z₃) − Z₃² = Z₁Z₂ + Z₁Z₃ + Z₂Z₃. With 2, 3, 4 Ω: 6 + 8 + 12 = 26 Ω², as found.

beyond: Not for the exam. At high frequency stray capacitance spoils an open circuit and lead inductance spoils a short, so engineers measure S parameters and convert. Circuit simulators build the Y matrix of the whole circuit by nodal analysis. Search for “nodal admittance matrix”.
